Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 29, verses 5–7:

His saying: ﴿Whoever hopes for the meeting with Allah﴾ has two interpretations.

One of them: "Whoever fears the meeting with Allah." This is the view of Ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi.

The second: "Whoever aspires to it" (yu'ammil).

Regarding ﴿the meeting with Allah﴾ there are two interpretations.

One of them: the reward of Allah. This is the view of Ibn Jubayr.

The second: being raised up to Him (al-ba'th ilayh). This is the view of Yahya ibn Salam.

﴿Indeed, the term of Allah is coming﴾: meaning the recompense on the Day of Resurrection, so prepare yourselves for it.

﴿And He is the All-Hearing﴾ of your speech.

﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of what you believe.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 29, verses 8–9:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We have enjoined upon man kindness to his parents﴾, has two interpretations:

One: its meaning is that We obligated him to do righteousness toward them. This was said by al-Suddi.

The second: that what We enjoined upon him of righteousness toward them is kindness (ḥusn).

﴿But if they strive with you﴾, i.e., they obligate you.

﴿To associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge﴾. Regarding this there are two interpretations:

One: that of which you have no proof, because proof (ḥujjah) is the path to knowledge (ʿilm).

The second: that you make for Me a partner, since no one has any knowledge of that.

﴿So do not obey them﴾. He commanded obedience to parents in obligatory matters, as a definite requirement, and in permissible matters as a recommendation, and He forbade obeying them in forbidden matters, as a decisive prohibition. It has come in a report: there is no obedience to a creature in disobedience to the Creator.

﴿To Me is your return﴾, meaning on the Day of Resurrection.

﴿Then I will inform you about what you used to do﴾, meaning in the world, of good for which reward is deserved and of evil for which punishment is warranted.

They differed concerning the occasion of its revelation, although its ruling is general, into two opinions:

One: it was revealed concerning Saʿd ibn Abi Waqqas, when his mother swore an oath concerning him and vowed that she would not eat food until he returned from the religion of Muhammad (ﷺ). This was said by Muṣʿab, Saʿd, and Qatadah.

The second: that it was revealed concerning ʿAyyash ibn Abi Rabiʿah.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 29, verses 14–15:

His saying, Most High: ﴿And We indeed sent Noah to his people﴾. Qatadah narrated from Anas that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The first prophet who was sent was Noah." Qatadah said: "He was sent from al-Jazirah."

﴿So he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years﴾. Concerning this there are four opinions:

The first: this is the full extent of his lifespan.

Qatadah said: He remained among them before he called them for three hundred years, and he called them for three hundred years, and he lived after the Flood three hundred and fifty years.

If it is asked, "Why did He say, ﴿a thousand years less fifty years﴾ and not say nine hundred and fifty years?" then there are two answers to this:

One of them: the purpose of it is to magnify the number, so mentioning the thousand was more grand in wording and greater in number.

The second: what is reported, that he was given a lifespan of a thousand years, and he gave fifty years of his lifespan to some of his offspring. When death came to him, he returned to seek completion of the thousand, so God mentioned that, as a reminder that the deficiency came from his side. This is one opinion.

The second opinion: that he was sent at forty years of his age, and remained among his people a thousand years (p-279) less fifty years, and lived after the Flood sixty years, so the full extent of his lifespan was a thousand years and fifty years. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas.

The third: that he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years, and lived after that seventy years, so the full extent of his lifespan was a thousand years and twenty years. This was said by Kaʿb al-Ahbar.

The fourth opinion: that he was sent when he was three hundred and fifty years old, and remained among his people calling them for a thousand years less fifty years, and lived after the Flood three hundred and fifty years, so the full extent of his lifespan was a thousand years and six hundred and fifty years. This was said by ʿAwn ibn Abi Shaddad.

﴿Then the flood seized them﴾. Concerning this there are three opinions:

The first: that the flood (ṭūfān) is rain. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Jubayr, Qatadah and al-Suddi.

The second: that the flood is drowning. This was said by al-Ḍaḥḥak.

The third: that it is death. ʿĀʾishah narrated it from the Prophet (ﷺ), and from it is the saying of the poet:

؎ Death's sweeping flood has consumed them

It is also said that the ṭūfān is every general calamity of harm.

Ismaʿil ibn ʿAbd Allah related that the flood took place in Nisan. (p-280)

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 29, verses 24–27:

(p-281) His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So Lut believed in him﴾. Ibn Ishaq said: Lut, who was the son of Ibrahim's brother, believed in Ibrahim, and Sarah, who was his paternal cousin, believed in him.

﴿And he said: Indeed I am emigrating to my Lord﴾. That is, I am emigrating away from the wrongdoers.

Regarding where he emigrated to, there are two opinions:

The first: He emigrated to Harran. This was said by Ka'b al-Ahbar.

The second: He emigrated from Kutha, which is in the outskirts of Kufa, to the land of Sham. This was said by Qatadah.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And We gave him his reward in this world﴾. Concerning this there are six sayings:

The first: It is good remembrance. This was said by Ibn Abbas.

The second: The approval of the people of the religions. This was said by Qatadah.

The third: The good intention through which he earned the reward in the Hereafter. This was said by al-Hasan.

The fourth: A tongue of truthfulness. This was said by Ikrimah.

The fifth: What he was given of reward in this world. This was narrated by Ibn Barzah.

The sixth: A righteous offspring. This was related by Ibn Isa, and said by al-Kalbi, to the extent that most of the prophets were from his descendants.

And it may be a seventh: that it is the continuation of prayer at his grave, and this is not for any other of the prophets.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 29, verses 28–30:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, you approach men⁠—﴾ meaning: you have intercourse with men (tankihūna al-rijāl).

﴿and cut off the path⁠﴾. Regarding this there are three opinions:

(p-282) First: it means highway robbery against the traveler. This was said by Ibn Zayd.

Second: by committing the abomination with men, they cut people off from travel out of fear of their vile deed. This was related by Ibn Shajara.

Third: it means cutting off offspring, by turning away from women to men. Wahb said: they became free of women through men.

﴿and commit the evil in your gatherings⁠﴾, meaning: in your assemblies (majālisikum). Regarding the evil (al-munkar) in this there are four opinions:

First: they used to break wind (yataḍarratūna) in their assemblies. This was reported by ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her.

Second: they used to pelt (yakhdhifūna) whoever passed by them with pebbles and mock him. This was narrated by Umm Hāni', from the Prophet (ﷺ).

Third: they used to have intercourse with men in their assemblies. This was transmitted by Manṣūr from Mujāhid.

Fourth: it is whistling, playing with pigeons, the slingshot (al-jalāhiq), lesbianism (al-siḥāq), and undoing the buttons of singing-girls (al-qiyān) in the assembly. This was narrated by al-Ḥākim from Mujāhid. (p-283)

﴿Like the spider that takes a house﴾ means that they worship what cannot benefit them at all, like a spider's house, which repels nothing. This is among the most eloquent parables about them.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 29, verses 44–45:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book﴾, meaning the Qur'an. This is an address to the Prophet ﷺ to recite to his community what has been sent down of it.

﴿And establish the prayer﴾. Concerning this there are three interpretations:

The first: that it means the Qur'an. This was said by Ibn ʿUmar.

The second: that it means the obligatory prayer (al-ṣalah al-mafrudah). This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas.

The third: that the prayer here is supplication (al-duʿaʾ), and its meaning is: stand up in supplication to the command of God. This was said by Ibn Bahr.

﴿Indeed, the prayer forbids immorality and wrongdoing﴾. Immorality (al-fahshaʾ) is fornication (al-zina), and wrongdoing (al-munkar) is polytheism (al-shirk). This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 29, verse 46:

The Most High says: ﴿And do not argue with the People of the Book except in a way that is best﴾. Concerning this there are three interpretations:

(p-286) The first: that ﴿the way that is best﴾ is the statement "There is no god but Allah." This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas.

The second: refraining from them when they offer the jizya (the poll-tax paid by non-Muslim subjects) and fighting them if they refuse. This was said by Mujahid.

The third: if they say something evil, then say to them something good. This was related by Ibn Abi Najih.

The second: it is said by one who has believed. This was said by al-Suddi.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 29, verses 47–49:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And you did not recite any scripture before it, nor did you write it with your right hand﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions:

The first: its meaning is ﴿And you did not recite any﴾ scripture before the Qur'an, any book of the books of God that was sent down, ﴿nor did you write it with your right hand﴾, that is, you did not write it, so that you would know what God had sent down in it, and then they might doubt your report about it, that it is revelation from God, Glorified is He, to you. This is the meaning of the saying of Yahya ibn Salam.

The second: the People of the Book would find in their scriptures that Muhammad does not write with his right hand and does not read a book. So this was revealed concerning them, to show them the soundness of his prophethood. This is the meaning of the saying of Mujahid.

﴿Otherwise, the falsifiers would have had cause for doubt﴾. Concerning them there are three sayings:

The first: they are the polytheists of Quraysh. This was said by Mujahid.

The second: the polytheists of the Arabs, who would say, "If he could read, he must have learned it from someone else." This was said by Qatadah.

The third: they are the deniers among the Jews. This was said by al-Suddi.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Rather, it is clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge﴾. Concerning this there are two opinions:

The first: it refers to the Prophet ﷺ, in that he was unlettered, neither writing nor reading. ﴿Clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge﴾ from among the People of the Book, because he is described in their scriptures with this attribute. This was said by al-Dahhak.

The second: it refers to the Qur'an, ﴿clear signs in the breasts of those who have been given knowledge﴾, and they are the Prophet ﷺ and the believers who follow him. This was said by al-Hasan.

Al-Hasan said: This community was given the gift of memorization, whereas those before them would not read their scripture except by looking at it, and when they closed it they would not retain what was in it, except for the prophets.

Ka'b said, describing this community: They are forbearing and learned, as if they were prophets in understanding.

﴿And none deny Our signs except the wrongdoers﴾. Ibn Abbas said: they are the polytheists.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 29, verse 50–52:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they say, "Why were no signs sent down to him from his Lord?"﴾ On this there are two opinions:

One: They were asking him for signs they proposed to him, as the polytheists of Quraysh did, such as that he turn al-Safa into gold and make a river flow in Makkah.

The second: They asked him for the like of the signs of the prophets before him, as Salih came with the she-camel, Musa with the staff, and Isa with the raising of the dead.

﴿Say, "Signs are only with Allah."﴾ That is, Allah is the One who gives whatever signs He wills to whichever prophets He wills, according to what He sees as beneficial. For this reason the signs of all the prophets did not coincide; rather, each prophet came with a type of them.

﴿And I am only a clear warner.﴾ He means that the Prophet (ﷺ) is charged with warning and clarification, not with what is proposed to him of signs. Rather, it is incumbent upon him to bring what attests to his truthfulness of miracles, and Allah has done that, so He answered them with it, saying:

﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book, being recited to them?﴾ He means the Qur'an is recited to them. On this there are two aspects:

One: Is it not sufficient for them, among the signs they asked for, that We have sent down to you the Book as a sign and proof of your truthfulness, due to its inimitability in its composition, the truthfulness of its reports, and the soundness of its promise?

The second: It is carried upon what 'Amr ibn Dinar narrated from Yahya ibn Ja'dah, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was brought a book written on a shoulder-blade, and he said: 'It is enough folly for a people that they turn away from what their prophet brought to another prophet, or from a book other than their book.' So Allah revealed: ﴿Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book, being recited to them?﴾"

﴿Indeed, in that is mercy and a reminder for a people who believe.﴾ He means their rescue from error, and by the reminder, their guidance to the truth.

﴿For a people who believe﴾ — that is, who desire faith and do not intend obstinacy.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say, "Allah is sufficient as a witness between me and you."﴾ He means a witness to truthfulness and delivery, while against you is denial and obstinacy.

﴿He knows what is in the heavens and the earth.﴾ This is an argument against them regarding the validity of His testimony concerning them, because they have acknowledged His knowledge, so it is binding upon them to acknowledge His testimony.

﴿And those who believed in falsehood﴾ — on this there are two aspects:

One: In Iblis; this was said by Yahya ibn Sallam.

The second: In the worship of idols and images; this was said by Ibn Shajarah.

﴿and disbelieved in Allah﴾ — this may have two meanings:

One: By their denial of His messengers and their rejection of His books.

The second: By what they associated with Him of gods, and what they attributed to Him of children and equals.

﴿It is those who are the losers.﴾ On this there are two aspects:

One: They lost their own selves by destroying them; this was said by 'Ali ibn 'Isa.

The second: They lost in the Hereafter the bliss of Paradise through the punishment of the Fire; this was said by Yahya ibn Sallam.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And they ask you to hasten the punishment﴾, concerning which there are two views:

﴿And had it not been for a specified term﴾, concerning which there are four sayings:

The first: it is the Day of Resurrection, as said by Ibn Jubayr.

The second: the term of life until the time of death, and the term of death until the time of resurrection to Him; "between two terms from Allah," as said by Qatadah.

The third: that it is the first blast (of the Trumpet), as said by Yahya ibn Sallam.

(p-291) His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is vast﴾. On this there are five interpretations:

First: Keep away from the people of sin by leaving their land. This was said by Ibn Jubayr and Ata'.

Second: Seek out the friends of God when they appear, by going out to them. This was said by Abu al-'Aliya.

Third: Strive against the enemies of God by fighting them. This was said by Mujahid.

Fourth: My mercy is vast for you. This was said by Mutarrif ibn Abd Allah.

Fifth: My provision is vast for you. This is also related from Mutarrif.

﴿So worship Me alone﴾. On this there are three interpretations:

First: "So fear Me." This was said by Bilal ibn Sa'd.

Second: "So worship Me" by emigrating to Madina. This was said by al-Suddi.

Third: "So worship Me" by not obeying anyone in disobedience to Me. This was said by Ali ibn Isa.

His saying: ﴿Every soul shall taste death﴾. On this there are two views:

One: It means that every living being is mortal.

Second: Seek out the friends of God when they appear, by going out to them. This was said by Abu al-'Aliya.

Third: Strive against the enemies of God by fighting them. This was said by Mujahid.

Fourth: My mercy is vast for you. This was said by Mutarrif ibn Abd Allah.

Fifth: My provision is vast for you. This is also related from Mutarrif.

﴿So worship Me alone﴾. On this there are three interpretations:

First: "So fear Me." This was said by Bilal ibn Sa'd.

Second: "So worship Me" by emigrating to Madina. This was said by al-Suddi.

Third: "So worship Me" by not obeying anyone in disobedience to Me. This was said by Ali ibn Isa.

His saying: ﴿Every soul shall taste death﴾. On this there are two views:

One: It means that every living being is mortal.

Two: That they will feel its distress and its severity. As for informing them of this, although they already know it, there are two reasons:

One: To frighten them with death so that they desist from sins.

Two: To make them know that the prophets of God, though specially honoured with His favour and singled out for His message, will still have death come upon them just as it comes upon others, so that they do not go astray when those among them die. Ja'far al-Sadiq related (p-292), from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: "When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) died, a visitor came to them whose voice they heard but whose person they did not see. He said: 'Peace be upon you, O People of the House, and the mercy of God and His blessings. ﴿Every soul shall taste death﴾. Indeed, in God there is consolation for every calamity, a substitute for everyone who perishes, and a recovery for everything lost. So place your trust in God, and hope in Him alone, for the one afflicted is he who is deprived of reward.'"

﴿Then to Us you will be returned﴾: this means the resurrection on the Day of Judgment after death in this world.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿We will surely settle them in the heights of Paradise, chambers﴾. Hamza and al-Kisa'i read (la-nathwiyannahum) with a thaʾ, from al-thiwa' which means prolonged residence, while the rest read it with a ba', ﴿la-nubawwi'annahum﴾, meaning: "We will surely lodge them in the upper parts of the houses."

He specified chambers for them for two reasons:

One: Chambers can only stand above houses, so in them there is a combination of two things.

Two: Because they are more pleasant than houses, owing to their elevation, and more agreeable to live in, owing to their breezes and their dryness.

Abu Malik al-Ash'ari related from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed in Paradise there are chambers whose outside can be seen from the inside, and whose inside can be seen from the outside. God has prepared them for those who feed the poor, speak goodly, persist in prayer and fasting, and stand in prayer at night while people are asleep."

His saying: ﴿And how many a creature does not carry its provision﴾. On this there are four sayings:

(p-293) First: Its meaning is that it eats with its mouth and carries nothing. This was said by Mujahid.

Second: It eats for its immediate time and does not store up for its tomorrow. This was said by al-Hasan.

Third: Its provision comes to it without seeking.

Fourth: It refers to the Prophet (ﷺ), who would eat and not store. This is related by al-Naqqash.

Ibn Abbas said: "Dawabb (creatures) means everything that crawls among animals."

None of them carries its provision or stores it, except the son of Adam, the ant, and the mouse.

﴿God provides for it and for you﴾: that is, He equalises between the eager one who trusts in God for his provision, the one who is content and desires what he has, and the strong and the weak alike, so that the strong does not deceive himself that he was provided for by his strength, and the weak does not imagine that he is prevented by his weakness.

Ibn Abbas said: This verse was revealed when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was permitted to emigrate and commanded the Muslims to do so. They feared loss and hunger, so some people said: "We would emigrate to a land where there is no livelihood." Then this verse was revealed, and they emigrated.

**Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on Surah 29, verses 64–66:**

His saying, the Exalted: "Indeed, the Hereafter – that is the [true] Life." Al-Dahhak said: it is the everlasting life. Abu 'Ubaydah said: al-hayawan (life) and al-hayah (life) are one and the same.

Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 29, verses 67–69:

(p-294) His saying: ﴿Have they not seen that We made a sanctuary secure, while people are being snatched away from around them?﴾ ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: It is Mecca, and they are the Quraysh, whom Allah made secure by it.

﴿While people are being snatched away from around them﴾ al-Dahhak said: some of them kill others and some of them take others captive. So Allah reminded them of this blessing so that they would submit to Him in obedience.

﴿Then in falsehood do they believe?﴾ Regarding this there are two interpretations:

First: Then in polytheism do they believe? This was said by Qatada.

Second: In Iblis (Satan). This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

﴿And in the blessing of Allah do they disbelieve?﴾ Regarding this there are four interpretations:

First: In the well-being (ʿafiyah) of Allah. This was said by Ibn ʿAbbas.

Second: In the gift and kindness of Allah. This was said by Ibn Shajara.

Third: In what the Prophet ﷺ brought of guidance. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

Fourth: In feeding them after hunger and securing them after fear. This was related by al-Naqqash, and this is an expression of wonder and denunciation that comes in the form of a question.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah or denies the truth when it has come to him?﴾ by ascribing to Allah a partner or a son.

﴿Or denies the truth when it has come to him﴾ Regarding this there are three interpretations:

First: With the Oneness (tawhid). This was said by al-Suddi.

Second: With the Qur'an. This was said by Yahya ibn Salam.

Third: With Muhammad ﷺ. This was said by Ibn Shajara.

﴿Is there not in Hell a residence (mathwa)?﴾ That is, a place of lasting abode.

His saying: ﴿And those who strive for Us﴾ Regarding this there are four interpretations:

First: They fought the polytheists obediently for Our sake.

Second: They struggled against their own souls in their desires out of fear of Us.

Third: They exerted themselves in acting in obedience and refraining from disobedience, seeking Our reward and fearing Our punishment.

Fourth: They struggled against their own souls in repenting of their sins.

(p-295) ﴿We shall surely guide them to Our paths﴾ Regarding this there are four interpretations:

First: It means the way to Paradise. This was said by al-Suddi.

Second: We shall grant them success toward the religion of truth. This was related by al-Naqqash.

Third: Its meaning is that those who act upon what they know, He guides to what they do not know. This was said by ʿAbbas Abu Ahmad.

Fourth: Its meaning is that We shall purify their intentions, their charities, their prayers, and their fasting. This was said by Yusuf ibn Asbat.

﴿And indeed Allah is with the doers of good﴾ That is, in aiding them. And Allah knows best.
